Every value in these widgets is computed exactly (with rational arithmetic, or from the checked format tables) and only rounded for display, so nothing you see here was
rounded by your browser's own floats.

## The 8-bit universe {#universe}

Eight bits give 256 codes, few enough to see every one. Pick a format, flip bits, click a value, or type
a number to see where it lands.

- **Our toy 1·4·3** uses the IEEE 754 rules: an all-ones exponent means ∞ or NaN.
- **FP8 E4M3** gives up ∞, keeps a single NaN pattern, and turns the top exponent into one more binade.
  That one rule change takes the largest value from 240 to 448.
- **FP8 E5M2** has the same layout as the top byte of an IEEE `binary16`.

::: {.column-page}

## Every format on one chart {#atlas}

From the 4-bit numbers inside AI chips to 256-bit giants. Right means more range, up means more precision.
Each extra exponent bit roughly doubles the range (counted in binades); each extra mantissa bit adds a bit of
precision. Click any format for its layout and limits.
